en: Now follows the majesty of the Karatoyā.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
"O Lord, let another thing be told, specifically concerning the rivers;
for the greatness of Pauṇḍrakṣetra has not been heard by me in detail, O Master."
O Lord of Beings, if you have grace toward me, I wish to hear: when is its origin, how does it come about, and from what specific cause? KtoM_02 //
By whom was that river Karajā manifested on earth,
and how was the auspicious and unsurpassed Pauṇḍra field flooded?
Īśvara said:
"O Goddess, at the time of your marriage, water was offered to you by Himavat;
it issued from my hand and fell upon the earth as nail-clippings."
O Goddess of the gods, everything concerning Pauṇḍra has already been told;
there itself, the fruit of Karatoyā was likewise described to you.
Even now, just as those [deities] and especially those rivers were revealed by Bhārgava as meritorious and removers of the sins of the Kali age.
Indeed, my son Guha also stays there at all times,
wherever the Lord Viṣṇu, the Sovereign whose vehicle is Garuḍa, resides.
Nārāyaṇa Hari is always present in every way in Pauṇḍra;
Brahmā does not leave Puṣkara, nor do I leave Vārāṇasī.
Keśava never abandons the sacred field of Śrī Pauṇḍravardhana,
the lotus-navel of the Earth, which has been purified by the waters from my hands.
Sūta said: Listen, all you sages, to that which was indeed spoken by Bhārgava,
having heard from Śaṅkara the words and the dialogue of both.
Out of affection for his son, it was revealed to Bhārgava;
that illustrious Bhārgava, in turn, made it known even to the sages.
Salutations to that Lord of Sages, the slayer of the lords of Dānavas;
salutations to you, Śrī Cakrapāṇi, whose very self is Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.
One [Parashurama], having slain the Kshatriyas in battle with nothing but his axe,
rendered the earth devoid of Kshatriyas twenty-one times over.
After that was Paraśurāma, whose prowess was renowned on earth;
the son of Jamadagni, possessed of great heroism, whose presence [endured] at the beginning of the Tretā age.
The omniscient one, of excellent vows, pure, the ordainer of all conduct,
with a heart drawn by curiosity— he is Hari, the supreme on earth.
In Pauṇḍra, on the highly meritorious and renowned Koṭiśilā island,
he offered the water of the Karatoyā river— purifying from beginning to end—
to the twice-born for the sake of the fruits of devotion and liberation.
For three days, a wondrous creation of gold was fashioned;
between Skanda and Govinda, the ground was prepared as a consecrated altar.
On the northern side of the middle of the altar stands the goddess Kālañjarī;
to her south is situated the goddess renowned as Koṭīśvarī.
In the southwest dwell ten million Liṅgas offered by Bhṛgu;
at Vāraṇa is Vijayā Caṇḍī, and in the north is Bhūtikeśvara.
Having bathed in that pool on an auspicious lunar day, a person is liberated from sin;
to the south of the deity Bhūtīkeśvara is the Sūryamaṇḍapa.
The sacrificial post (yūpa) placed in the center of the altar grows through its union with the people;
to the east of the Govinda pavilion is the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) fashioned by Viṣṇu.
To the northwest of the Skanda pavilion is the wonderful assembly hall of Rāma,
where there reside one hundred and twenty-five thousand Brahmins of marvelous deeds.
O Goddess, by the power of the asceticism of that great-souled lord of sages,
a pit created by Īśvara appeared in the northwestern corner of his assembly hall.

I bow my head to the city of Śrī Pauṇḍravardhana, the foremost abode on earth, inhabited by a hundred thousand and a quarter Brahmins and by gods such as Skanda, Viṣṇu, Balabhadra, and Śiva— a place where sins are washed away by the water used for their ritual hand-washing.
In the western part of Karajā, the Jāhnavī always flows;
but in the eastern part of Karajā, the water of the Jāhnavī is three-quarters less.
On the western bank of the Karatoyā, where the earth is red,
is declared the field of liberation (muktikṣetra), which destroys even the greatest of sins.
Having reached the Karatoyā river, a man who fasts for three nights obtains the merit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice and goes to the world of Śakra;
right here, having attained knowledge, he shall reach union with Hari.
Those who, having reached the Karatoyā river, cast off their bodies here;
There is no doubt that their liberation will occur as long as fourteen Indras endure.
Those who drink from the Devikā, the Karatoyā, and the sin-destroying Vipāśā—those are not humans; they are gods. (KtoM 29)
Between Skanda and Govinda, on a Monday coinciding with the new moon day,
he who bathes at dawn while observing silence shall deliver ten million members of his lineage.
How many particles of dust are there on the earth, and how vast is that which arises from space?
Indeed, it is impossible to describe the majesty of the Karatoyā.
Whatever fruit one might obtain by bathing in the waters of the Karatoyā at the time of the Mahājyaiṣṭhī festival through visiting Puruṣottama, that same fruit one obtains [by other means].
If the new moon (Kuhū) occurs in conjunction with the Moon while reaching the waters of the Karatoyā at the time of dawn,
it is equal to hundreds of solar eclipses.
Having reached Śilādvīpa, that [merit] becomes ten-millionfold;
and it becomes ten-millionfold again on a Sunday coinciding with the full moon of the month of Pauṣa.
Whatever merit is found at Vārāṇasī and Kurukṣetra during a lunar eclipse,
that shall become ten millionfold upon reaching Śilādvīpa.
If the new moon (Kuhū) is conjoined with the Moon during the month of Pauṣa or Māgha,
it becomes multiplied by ten million times ten million due to its conjunction with the Vyatīpāta yoga.
If the new moon (Kuhū) is conjoined with Mūla and the Sun is in the sign of Sagittarius (Cāpa), it is renowned as Nārāyaṇī; it shall deliver thirty million ancestors from bondage.
A worship performed in Vārāṇasī bestows its fruit in full;
however, it is said to be twice as efficacious when performed in the waters of the Karatoyā river.
And at Dvārāvatī, at the Gaṇḍakī, at Prayāga, and likewise at Puṣkara;
The worship that yields fruit at Kurukṣetra, known as Badarī,
is said to be four times more efficacious when performed in the waters of the Karatoyā river.
O Goddess, the worship of Viṣṇu in the waters of the Karatoyā is especially meritorious;
even greater than that is the abundance of fruit resulting from the worship of Śiva and Śakti together.
O Goddess, at the beginning of the month of Karkaṭaka, the Gaṅgā remains in her menses for three days; all rivers carrying blood flow, as does the river that carries the waters of the Karatoyā.
This goddess Śrīsundarī is remembered as the one who always flows with water.
O Queen of the Gods, for those who always perform their ablutions here and always offer libations, what need is there for much speaking? Liberation stands within the grasp of their hands.
Oh, how great is the majesty of this water arising from my very hand—
meritorious, removing the sins of men, and bestowing liberation through bathing and drinking!
If one makes one's dwelling on the bank of the Karatoyā River, that residence is equal to Vārāṇasī; such a person is liberated from sins.
O Goddess, O beautiful one, on the bank of the Karajā, worship of the deity accomplishes all aims;
other than this worship, O Goddess, there is no doubt.
Those who have died while the water of the Kāratoya remains within their bellies will attain liberation without a doubt for as long as fourteen Indras endure;
having attained knowledge right there, their liberation shall be absolute and stainless.
"O beautiful one, the water of both the Gaṅgā and the Karajā is here;
it is meritorious, removing all sins, and the most excellent purifier on earth."
O you whose wealth is austerity, he upon whose fingernail bones, hair,
and so forth fall shall attain heaven for as long as the fourteen Indras endure.
On the western bank of the Karatoyā, the Jāhnavī flows eternally;
there is a special place where the Lohinī river meets it, and its clay bestows liberation.
On the western bank of the Karatoyā, where the earth is red,
is declared to be the Field of Liberation (muktikṣetra), which destroys even the greatest sins.
The water of the Karatoyā is meritorious, purifying, and difficult to find on earth;
having bathed there for the entire month of Māgha, one shall go to the city of Viṣṇu.
On the bank of the Karatoyā river,
by performing Vedic worship and recitation and merely feeding Brahmins, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
In the city of Pauṇḍra, the merit becomes ten million times ten millionfold;
by feeding a single brāhmaṇa alone, one obtains the fruit of all sacrifices.
O beautiful one, through recitation, fire-offerings, as well as gifts, worship, ancestral rites, and other such acts,
the merit there in the Pauṇḍra-kṣetra is multiplied by tens of millions upon tens of millions.
And those who indeed wear a sectarian mark made from the clay of the Karatoyā river;
Assuming the form of Viṣṇu, they release [devotees] from sins; there is no doubt in this matter.
Between Skanda and Govinda lies the hidden city of Vārāṇasī;
by merely ascending there, a man becomes Nārāyaṇa.
This field is proclaimed to extend five *krośas* all around;
within it, O Maheśvarī, is this [inner] space of one *krośa*,
a most secret field where the sage Bhārgava resides.
Guha tells of the knowledge regarding the animal: in that house, there is a copper-crested cock; a long golden staff fashioned with a fragrant [handle] and increasing in size; a stone and a bone;
an umbrella that does not open in the sky; a snake; a world of living beings with two vowels; a well; an island; and the falling of gold—these are the wonders in the Pauṇḍra field.
The ground becomes excellent through bathing in the Taruṇa and Kāmyaka pools; there, enjoyment, sacrifice, wandering, and dancing take place, for the Veda is indeed the spoken word.
Thus Rāma established nineteen characteristics; therefore, this is renowned throughout all the worlds as the Śrī Mahāsthāna.
May that city of Pauṇḍra protect you—where the river Śrīpāṇitoyā destroys the mass of sins through its bathing; where every human bone situated within it attains the state of a stone;
where even the god who slays Tāraka bestows most wonderful knowledge; and where the water from the well becomes as abundant as oil.
[Comm: c. adbhutaṃ: corrected;
adbhūtaṃ in the edition] Thus ends the majesty of Pauṇḍra-kṣetra in the Uttarapauṇḍra-khaṇḍa.
Sūta said:
Listen, all you sages, to the greatness of that water;
on this bank of the Bāhudā, every drop of water removes all impurities.
There is no difference here between the Gaṅgā and the Karatoyā;
the Gaṅgā is that which rests upon the head of Hara, while the other has issued forth from his hand.

"O Karatoyā, you of constant waters, most excellent and renowned of rivers, you who perpetually flood the Pauṇḍras; O you born from the hand, remove my sin!"—with this mantra one should indeed bathe in the auspicious waters of the Karatoyā. (KtoM 63)
There is no river whatsoever whose form is equal to yours, since you are free from dust;
you are blessed, you are meritorious, you are the best of rivers—salutations to you, who have your origin in the hand of Śrīkaṇṭha.
From bathing in this water of [the Lord’s] fingernails, one destroys misfortunes; here, the Blessed One, the destroyer of saṃsāra, bestows knowledge.
In ancient times, from the munificent sage Likhita came the Bāhudā;
she is ever-flowing, highly meritorious, cool-streaming, and auspicious.
The sages and seers, the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya,
Aśvatthāman, the best of monkeys (Hanumān), and Vāsudeva himself, the all-pervading Lord.
Caturmukha, Pañcamukha, Karimukha, and Ṣaṇmukha—
all of them are on the western side, on the bank of the river Karatoyā.
For the sake of ascetic penance, those who are free from passion and seekers of the waterless state remain there;
they are devoid of dust, possess great merit, and are distinguished as lions among men in the solar age.
O beautiful one, by the mere act of reaching the waters of the Karatoyā river,
bathing and libations must necessarily be performed until its further bank.
For one who goes to the other shore without bathing, there would be a loss of previously acquired merit;
but having bathed and likewise drunk water, one does not defile either this shore or the far shore.
The highly meritorious Pauṇḍra-kṣetra was flooded by waters originating from the hand;
merely by bathing in that water, one increases the pleasure of Viṣṇu.
Two yojanas to the north of Pauṇḍrakṣetra, in that interval,
dwells the goddess Caṇḍikā, where the earth is red.
At that ford, by the mere power of prayer, the goddess Caṇḍikā bestows horses and palaces upon people on the bank of the Karatoyā river;
oh, through the majesty of this sacred field, she removes even the sin of killing a Brahmin!
[COMM: a. taddhāre: Is this the intended reading? Or taddhari?
The printing is unclear.]
Water from a sacred bathing place (*tīrtha*) that has been touched by a *cāṇḍāla* or an outcaste (*antyaja*) is not purifying,
unless it is the water of the Karajā, Gaṅgā, Narmadā, or Yamunā.
Those men who perform their ablutions even with water brought in vessels are released from the flood of their sins without exception; of this there is no doubt.
Whatever man bathes in the waters of the Karatoyā, whether with knowledge or without it,
attains the world of Brahmā, having indeed destroyed the sins of the day.
Even those men of wicked conduct who, though unknowingly, drink the water from the tips of the fingers even once, become free from sin.
In this very city of Pauṇḍra, there is the accomplishment of the goals of human life; Vārāṇasī is merely a source of calamity for men.
Right here is the abode of Viṣṇu, the entirety of sacrifice, knowledge, various forms of meditative absorption, and the attainment of perfection through the practice of recitation.
The Kṛṣṇaveṇī, the Tāmraparṇī, the Sarayū, and likewise the Gaṇḍakī;
the holy Yamunā and the Sarasvatī, which both originate from the foot of Viṣṇu.
The Kāverī, Kauśikī, Candrabhāgā, Ciravallabhī,
Svarṇā, Campā, Vetravatī, as well as the Ātreyī and Punarbhavā.
Vipāpā and Vipāśā, Citrā and Citrotpalā,
as well as Gotamī, Gomukhī, Revā, and the long-lasting Sarasvatī.
O beloved, all the rivers dwelling upon the earth and all masses of water are always present within the water of my hand. (KtoM 83)
Having recited this in Pauṇḍradvīpa, the venerable sage Vīra Bhārgava circumambulated the Pauṇḍras and was liberated from the sin of killing a Brahmin.

The man who, being pure, recites the majesty of the great sacred ford of Karatoyā at the three junctions of the day, or even at a single junction, or who listens to it with his mind fixed upon that [ford],
shall enjoy all pleasures in this world and, with his thoughts directed toward that [ford], [attain the supreme goal].
Having passed away, he goes to the supreme state, which wards off all impurities.
Thus ends the glorification of the Karatoyā composed by Paraśurāma, within the Uttarapauṇḍrakhaṇḍa, in the dialogue between Sūta and Śaunaka.
